  Terse gloss: "A queen; a woman who reigns or holds royal authority"
  Readable gloss: "The feminine noun basílissa designates a woman who holds royal power or sovereignty, whether as reigning monarch or queen consort. In the Synoptic Gospels, Jesus invokes the 'Queen of the South' — the Queen of Sheba — who traveled to hear Solomon's wisdom, shaming his unresponsive generation (Matt 12:42; Luke 11:31). In Acts 8:27, the Ethiopian eunuch serves Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. Revelation 18:7 uses it of Babylon's self-exaltation: 'I sit as a queen.' Spanish 'reina,' French 'reine,' and German 'Königin' all preserve the straightforward royal feminine sense."

  Sense 1: ""
